scope: Bound named dictionary object setter staging before caller-owned data is copied or moved into the DXF writer.

behavior: Both const-vector and rvalue setNamedDictObjects overloads reject vectors above DRW_Dictionary::kMaxEntries before copying or moving them.
Rejected setter input marks the pending named dictionary state invalid, so writeObjects refuses before emitting bytes rather than serializing stale objects.
The const-vector setter copies into a temporary and swaps only after successful allocation; allocation failure marks input rejected.
A later valid setter call clears the rejection state, allowing corrected same-codec retry.

focused.coverage: ASCII/Binary count refusal for root and named dictionary setters, caller/prior-state preservation, no output change, corrected same-codec retry, and existing rooted IMAGEDEF adapter closure.

limitations: The 100,000-object ceiling is an internal resource limit, not a DXF format maximum or support claim.
The selector proves setter admission and failure/retry state; it does not qualify named dictionary serialization semantics, aggregate nested-entry work, or native consumer behavior.
Other staging/assembly paths, allocation-failure injection, rollback after earlier staged records, source lifetime and platform policy remain open.
next: Continue the safety and caller-state audit on other unbounded setup/assembly paths, rollback after earlier staged records, source lifetime, platform numeric/string policies and scoped concurrency.
